liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Brokedowm Palace (4)** (2 reviews): The Brokedown encore comes from an inferior soundboard source, not an audience recording, according to reviewer [23][24]
- **Loser** (1 review): Reviewer names Loser among the musical highlights, along with Johnny B. Goode and the second set from the jam into drums onward [20]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Reviewer says Garcia's solo is outstanding, with an unusually fat, rich, clean guitar tone [18]
- **Iko Iko (2)** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed the Iko Iko and the Memphis Blues [18]
- **The Other One (4)** (1 review): Reviewer says it never gets airborne, with the band holding back [15]
- **Stella Blue (4)** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Stella Blue into Brokedown Palace section with Ornette Coleman as especially soulful [14]
- **Turn On YourLovelight (4)** (1 review): Reviewer hears some funk in it, but says it only digs in near the end [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-02-23.sbd.unknown.14485.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 170 min; rated 3.17/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1993-02-23.116152.NeumannKMF4.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 148 min; rated 3/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1993-02-23.142895.mtx.tobin.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 172 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd93-02-23.sbd.hall.1611.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 168 min; rated 4.04/5 by 23 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer grades the sound an A; Reviewer finds sound quality and mix excellent, with the band's enjoyment audible through the line; Reviewer calls the recording snappy and pulsating, very good for the era [14][17][21]
- **gd1993-02-23.134784.neumann.fob.jbraveman.flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 172 min [8]. Said about its sound: Excellent front-of-board-area recording with no major glitches; set one was recorded hotter, so its volume was lowered to match set two [8]

## Around the show

- Ornette Coleman sat in but, per the reviewer, never really meshed with the band; Space felt empty [15]
- Attendee asks about the yellow guitar Garcia played in the second set, which they had not noticed before [16]
- Parade included a huge Bill Clinton float holding a sax in one hand and a joint in the other, smoke pouring from his head [19]
- Reviewer enjoyed the Ornette set despite the sound [19]
- A winding path opened on the floor so parade floats could pass while drummers played; giant sax-playing, joint-smoking Clinton float [20]
- Reviewer says Garcia played his guitar 'Wolf' for this show [20]
- Reviewer says Garcia played Wolf all night, and Phil had a loud, bouncy lead bass tone [23]
- Reviewer says Garcia played Wolf all night, and Phil had a loud, bouncy lead bass tone [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-02-23.sbd.unknown.14485.shnf**: source: SBD>DAT(S)>CDR [1]. Also: Reviewer says this sounds like a genuine DAT soundboard, unlike the other source, which seems to include a cassette generation; Soundboard transfer; Brokedown Palace is taken from an audience source [1][23]
- **gd1993-02-23.116152.NeumannKMF4.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 2 Neumann KMF4 microphones-up front > Sony TC-D5M - analog master cassettes; [2]
- **gd1993-02-23.142895.mtx.tobin.flac1644**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (shnid = 1611) SBD> DAT> Sonic Solutions (for phase correction)> CD; via Mike Hall + AUD (shnid = 141067) fl1c6/44.1 Source Info: FOB… [3]. Also: Matrix mixing a soundboard and audience source, made by an archive.org user, 44/16 FLAC [3]
- **gd93-02-23.sbd.hall.1611.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> DAT> Sonic Solutions (for phase correction)> CD [5]. Also: Reviewer says this sounds like a genuine DAT soundboard, unlike the other source, which seems to include a cassette generation [24]
- **gd1993-02-23.134784.neumann.fob.jbraveman.flac1648**: taped by unknown; transferred by jbraveman; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source: Neumann TLM 170 FOB AUD > DAT; [8]. Also: Neumann microphone recording, processed in Goldwave to remove close claps and balloon pops [8]
